comment: The decisions any catalog has to make, whatever it catalogs. This file exists because of docs/service-split-handoff.md section 2.1: asked an open question, the non-thinking model answers with whatever the prompt made salient and silently skips the rest -- in the measured case, 4 categories of 8. A reasoning model walks a list like this in its scratchpad; this one has to be handed it. So the model never generates the dimensions, only decides which apply to the subject and what the field's own vocabulary calls them. 'often_missed' marks the ones a model reaches for last; 'enumeration_clause' names those explicitly in the prompt, because naming the omission is what moved the numbers, not listing the full set.
enumeration_clause: Work through the dimensions in order and ask what this field does about each one before moving on. Do not stop at identification, description, and classification: a catalog also has to settle naming authority, provenance and acquisition, condition and state, measurement and units, identifiers issued by outside registries, legal and ethical constraints, the split between a reference record and an event record, and what is kept versus discarded. A dimension this field genuinely does not have is a legitimate answer; say so rather than inventing practice for it.

dimensions.label: Identity and naming authority
dimensions.question: What names one of these unambiguously, and who decides the correct name?
dimensions.why: Fields with a nomenclatural authority (binomial names, IMA mineral names, MARC authority files) have a right answer and a citation for it. A vault that stores the popular name loses the join to every outside record.
dimensions.vault_note: Usually the note title convention, in the existing wiki form 'Canonical Name, Gloss'.

dimensions.label: Classification hierarchy
dimensions.question: What formal hierarchy or controlled taxonomy do practitioners file these under?
dimensions.why: Distinguishes a genuine storage boundary from a topical label. Most hierarchies belong in the note body or in links, not in the folder tree.
dimensions.vault_note: A hierarchy is rarely a subdomain. Folder depth is capped at domain/subdomain/project.

dimensions.label: Identification and description
dimensions.question: What does a practitioner record to tell one of these from a similar one?
dimensions.why: The core of a reference card and the section a field guide is actually good at.
dimensions.vault_note: Managed body sections in the kind spec.

dimensions.label: Provenance and acquisition
dimensions.question: Where did this specimen, copy, or record come from, and how is that chain recorded?
dimensions.why: Museums, archives, and libraries treat provenance as load-bearing; a hobby catalog usually invents it late and badly.
dimensions.vault_note: Often a body table on the record note rather than a property.

dimensions.label: Temporal facts
dimensions.question: Which dates matter, and do any of them recur or vary by season?
dimensions.why: A recurring window is a different fact from a one-off date and cannot be stored the same way.
dimensions.vault_note: One-off dates use the existing `date` property. Recurring windows are a managed body table, the way Phenology is.

dimensions.label: Spatial facts
dimensions.question: Does place change what is true about one of these, or only where it was found?
dimensions.why: If a fact varies by region, storing it without its region makes it a fact about nowhere.
dimensions.vault_note: Region-scoped rows in a body table, keyed to a wiki `place` note.

dimensions.label: Condition and state
dimensions.question: Does one of these have a condition, grade, or lifecycle state that practitioners record on a scale?
dimensions.why: Graded fields (philately, numismatics, book collecting, conservation) have published scales; a free-text guess is worthless next to one.
dimensions.vault_note: A controlled column in a body table. Not a `status` value -- `status` is the note's lifecycle, not the object's.

dimensions.label: Measurement and units
dimensions.question: What is measured, in what units, and to what precision?
dimensions.why: Units left implicit are the classic silent corruption; a field with a standard usually names one.
dimensions.vault_note: Units belong in the column heading, not in each cell.

dimensions.label: Media, specimens, and physical holdings
dimensions.question: Is there a photograph, specimen, recording, or physical object, and how is it referenced?
dimensions.why: A catalog whose records point at nothing is a reading list.
dimensions.vault_note: Attachments live under the Meta attachments route; `cover` is human-owned and never set by tooling.

dimensions.label: External registry identifiers
dimensions.question: Which outside registries issue an identifier for one of these, and which is canonical?
dimensions.why: The single highest-value field for later federation, and the one a model asked for 'good metadata' almost never proposes.
dimensions.vault_note: A body table row or a Sources link. It is not worth a global frontmatter property.

dimensions.label: Relationships between records
dimensions.question: What typed relationships do practitioners draw between two of these?
dimensions.why: Decides what belongs in `related`/`parent` versus what needs its own note.
dimensions.vault_note: The vault has `parent`, `related`, `people`, and `organization`. No new link property is available.

dimensions.label: Reference record versus event record
dimensions.question: Does this field keep a durable card about the kind of thing, separate from a dated record of one encounter?
dimensions.why: The single most consequential structural decision, and the one the species feature turned on: a species card and a sighting are not the same note and must not share a route.
dimensions.vault_note: A reference card is a wiki subdomain; an event record is its own domain.

dimensions.label: Legal, ethical, and safety constraints
dimensions.question: Is any of this regulated, protected, dangerous, or sensitive to publish?
dimensions.why: Protected-species localities, human remains, culturally restricted material, and edibility claims all have practice around them that a generic schema silently violates.
dimensions.vault_note: Usually an owner-owned section the pipeline never writes, the way edibility is on fungus cards.

dimensions.label: Retention and curation
dimensions.question: What does a practitioner discard, correct, or supersede, and how is that recorded?
dimensions.why: A catalog with no notion of a superseded record accumulates contradictions.
dimensions.vault_note: The existing `status` values usually cover this. Check before proposing anything.
